name: Tamar (Judah's daughter-in-law)
title: The Righteous Widow
summary: Tamar was a Canaanite woman who married Judah's eldest son, Er. After both Er and his brother Onan died, she took matters into her own hands to secure her right to descendants. She became the mother of the twins Perez and Zerah, and is one of four women mentioned in Jesus' lineage.

keyEvents.title: Marriage to Er
keyEvents.description: Tamar was married to Judah's eldest son, Er, but the Lord caused him to die because he was wicked.

keyEvents.title: Duty of the Daughter-in-Law with Onan
keyEvents.description: Judah gave Tamar to his second son, Onan, to fulfill the duty of a daughter-in-law, but Onan refused to give her children and also died.

keyEvents.title: Sent back to her father's house
keyEvents.description: Judah sent Tamar home as a widow with the promise that she would marry his youngest son Shelah when he grew up, but he did not keep his word.

keyEvents.title: The Disguise at Timnah
keyEvents.description: When Tamar realized Judah would not give her to Shelah, she disguised herself as a prostitute and waited for him on the road to Timnah.

keyEvents.title: The Revelation and Justification
keyEvents.description: When Judah intended to punish her for immorality, she showed his seal, cord, and staff as proof. Judah declared that she was more righteous than he.

keyEvents.title: The Birth of Perez and Zerah
keyEvents.description: Tamar gave birth to twins, and Perez became an ancestor in the lineage of David and Jesus.
